title: AWS Cloud-Native E-Commerce Platform
description: Production-oriented Cloud and DevOps architecture case study for designing a scalable, secure and observable cloud-native e-commerce platform on AWS. The architecture demonstrates independently deployable services, Infrastructure as Code, containerized workloads, automated CI/CD, private networking, managed AWS services, security controls, observability and reliability engineering practices.
executive_summary: Designed a production-oriented AWS cloud-native architecture for a scalable e-commerce platform using independently deployable services, containerized workloads, managed AWS services, Infrastructure as Code, automated delivery, secure networking, observability and reliability engineering practices. The project is presented as a technical architecture and portfolio case study and does not claim that the complete platform is currently deployed to a production AWS account.

architecture.overview: The platform uses Amazon CloudFront and Route 53 as the public entry layer, API Gateway and Application Load Balancer for API routing, Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate for containerized application workloads, DynamoDB and Amazon RDS for data persistence, and SQS/SNS for asynchronous communication. Supporting AWS services provide container image management, authentication, object storage, observability and access control.
request_flow: User accesses the e-commerce platform through the application domain
Amazon Route 53 resolves the application domain
Amazon CloudFront provides the content delivery layer
Static frontend content is served from Amazon S3
API requests are routed through Amazon API Gateway
API Gateway forwards application traffic toward the Application Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer routes requests to ECS services
Amazon ECS runs containerized microservices using AWS Fargate
Microservices communicate with their respective data and messaging services
Application responses are returned through the API and CDN layers
service_flow: Payment Service integrates with external payment capabilities
Catalog Service uses DynamoDB for scalable catalog-oriented persistence
Order Service uses Amazon RDS for relational transactional data
Application notifications can be distributed using Amazon SNS
Amazon CloudWatch provides logs, metrics and alarms

frontend_architecture.description: The frontend is designed as a static web application distributed through Amazon CloudFront with Amazon S3 providing object and static content storage.
benefits: Separation of frontend and backend workloads

api_architecture.description: Application APIs are exposed through a managed API entry layer and routed to containerized backend services.
benefits: Improved separation between public API access and internal workloads

containerization.description: Application services are packaged as Docker containers and deployed to Amazon ECS using AWS Fargate.
workflow: Image is pushed to Amazon ECR
ECS task definition references the image
ECS service deploys the new container version using Fargate

infrastructure_as_code.description: Terraform is used as the Infrastructure as Code layer for defining and managing the AWS platform.
engineering_benefits: Improved disaster recovery and environment reconstruction

networking.description: The architecture separates public-facing components from private application and data workloads using AWS networking controls.
design_principles: Public access is restricted to required entry points
Application workloads are isolated within controlled network boundaries
Databases should not be directly exposed to the public internet
Least-privilege network access is applied between components
Outbound connectivity is controlled according to workload requirements

security.description: Security is designed using AWS identity, network and workload isolation principles.
controls: Security groups with restricted inbound access
Secrets management for sensitive application configuration
Infrastructure changes managed through code review
security_principles: Separation of application and data layers

identity_and_access.description: IAM provides AWS-level identity and access control while Amazon Cognito provides customer-facing application authentication.
components: AWS IAM users and roles where required
principles: Separate deployment permissions from runtime permissions
Use short-lived authentication for CI/CD where possible

data_architecture.description: The platform uses different persistence technologies based on application workload characteristics rather than forcing every service onto a single database technology.

components.use_case: Product catalog and high-scale key-value/document access patterns.
Transactional relational data such as orders and strongly consistent relational workflows.
Static content, objects and application assets.

principles: Select storage based on workload requirements
Keep service data ownership clearly defined
Use managed AWS database services where appropriate
Design backup and recovery strategies for persistent workloads

messaging.description: Amazon SQS and SNS provide asynchronous communication patterns to reduce coupling between services and support event-driven workflows.

components.purpose: Queues asynchronous work and decouples producers from consumers.
Distributes notifications or events to multiple subscribers.

observability.description: Amazon CloudWatch provides centralized visibility into application and infrastructure health.

reliability.description: The platform incorporates reliability engineering principles through managed services, workload isolation, health checks, asynchronous processing and automated deployment practices.
principles: Use managed AWS services where appropriate
Run multiple application tasks for critical services
Use health checks for service availability
Use dead-letter queues for failed asynchronous messages

ci_cd.description: The application delivery model uses Git-based development, automated CI, container image publishing and automated deployment to ECS.
workflow: Application tests and validation are executed
Container image security checks are performed
Image is pushed to Amazon ECR
ECS service deploys the new application version
Health checks and deployment validation are performed

deployment_strategy.description: Containerized services are independently deployable on Amazon ECS, allowing individual microservices to be updated without requiring a full application deployment.

scalability.description: The architecture is designed to scale application services independently according to workload demand.
strategies: RDS scaling based on workload requirements
principles: Use managed services for elastic capacity
Avoid unnecessary coupling between application components

performance.description: Performance is addressed through content caching, independent service scaling, asynchronous processing and workload-specific data stores.

disaster_recovery.description: The platform is designed with managed-service backup and recovery capabilities as part of the reliability strategy.
considerations: Container images retained in Amazon ECR

operational_workflow: Container image is built and scanned
Image is pushed to Amazon ECR
Alerts are generated for operational issues
Failed deployments can be rolled back to a previous image

engineering_decisions.reason: Provides managed container orchestration while reducing operational overhead associated with managing container hosts.
Provides an AWS-native container registry integrated with ECS and IAM.
Separates static content delivery from backend workloads and provides scalable global content distribution.

engineering_decisions.decision: API Gateway and Application Load Balancer
engineering_decisions.reason: Provides a managed API entry point and controlled routing to containerized backend services.
Provides scalable NoSQL access patterns suitable for catalog-oriented workloads.
Provides managed relational database capabilities for transactional application data.
Decouples services, supports asynchronous processing and improves resilience for background workflows.
Provides managed customer authentication and reduces the need to build identity infrastructure from scratch.
Provides reproducible, version-controlled and reviewable AWS infrastructure.
Provides centralized logs, metrics and alarms across the application and AWS infrastructure.

challenges: Designing a scalable architecture without creating unnecessary operational complexity
Separating microservices while maintaining reliable service-to-service communication
Protecting application and database workloads from unnecessary public exposure
Selecting the appropriate AWS managed service for each workload
Balancing scalability, reliability, security and cost
Designing automated delivery while maintaining deployment safety
Providing a practical disaster recovery and rollback strategy
solutions: Used ECS and Fargate to provide managed container orchestration.
Used CloudFront and S3 to separate static frontend delivery from backend application workloads.
Used API Gateway and Application Load Balancer to provide controlled API and service routing.
Used DynamoDB and RDS according to different application data requirements.
Used SQS and SNS to decouple asynchronous workflows.
Applied private networking and security groups to reduce unnecessary public exposure.
Used IAM roles and least-privilege policies for workload and deployment access.
Used Terraform to manage infrastructure as code.
Used GitHub Actions to automate application validation, image builds and deployment.
Used CloudWatch for centralized monitoring, logs, metrics and alarms.
Designed health checks, retries, backups and rollback procedures as part of the reliability model.
lessons_learned: Cloud-native architecture is primarily about selecting appropriate managed services and defining clear service boundaries.
Independent deployment requires strong API and data ownership boundaries.
Container orchestration should reduce operational complexity rather than introduce unnecessary infrastructure management.
Security should be designed into networking, IAM, containers and application delivery rather than added later.
Asynchronous messaging can improve resilience and reduce coupling between services.
Observability is essential for operating distributed applications.
Infrastructure as Code provides a foundation for repeatability and disaster recovery.
Automated CI/CD improves delivery speed but must be combined with health checks and rollback mechanisms.
Scalability, security, reliability and cost should be considered together during architecture design.
Managed AWS services can significantly reduce operational overhead when selected according to workload requirements.
portfolio_highlights: Designed a cloud-native AWS architecture for an e-commerce platform.
Applied microservice-oriented application design with independently deployable services.
Designed containerized workloads using Amazon ECS and AWS Fargate.
Integrated Amazon ECR for container image management.
Designed S3 and CloudFront architecture for scalable frontend delivery.
Designed API Gateway and Application Load Balancer routing.
Applied DynamoDB and RDS for workload-specific data persistence.
Designed asynchronous communication using SQS and SNS.
Implemented IAM and private networking security principles.
Designed CloudWatch-based observability and reliability practices.
Documented disaster recovery, rollback and operational considerations.
challenges_summary: The primary architectural challenge was designing a scalable e-commerce platform that could independently deploy services while maintaining strong security, reliable communication, operational visibility and controlled infrastructure management. The design also needed to balance AWS managed services, application scalability, database requirements, asynchronous processing, cost and operational complexity.
solution_summary: The solution uses Route 53 and CloudFront at the edge, API Gateway and an Application Load Balancer for application traffic, ECS/Fargate for containerized microservices, DynamoDB and RDS for workload-specific persistence, SQS/SNS for asynchronous communication, Cognito for customer authentication, ECR for container images and CloudWatch for observability. Terraform provides Infrastructure as Code while GitHub Actions provides the foundation for automated CI/CD.
project_disclaimer: This project is a technical architecture and portfolio case study. It demonstrates the engineering approach, design decisions and implementation patterns for a cloud-native AWS e-commerce platform. It does not claim that the complete architecture is currently deployed to a production AWS account.
